desc: Udaipur Solar Observatory is a solar observatory located on an island in Fateh Sagar Lake, Udaipur, Rajasthan. Established in 1975 by the Physical Research Laboratory, it is one of the best solar observing sites in Asia. The observatory specializes in high-resolution observations of the solar photosphere and chromosphere. It houses a 15-cm refracting telescope and a 50-cm solar magnetograph. The lake's stable air provides excellent seeing conditions for solar observation. The observatory is part of the Global Oscillation Network Group (GONG) and contributes to international solar monitoring programs.
fact: It is located on an island in Fateh Sagar Lake, Udaipur · It was established in 1975 by the Physical Research Laboratory · It is one of the best solar observing sites in Asia · It is part of the Global Oscillation Network Group (GONG)

desc: The Indian Astronomical Observatory (IAO) is one of the world's highest astronomical observatories, located at Hanle in Ladakh at an altitude of 4,500 meters. Operated by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, it houses the 2-meter Himalayan Chandra Telescope. The telescope is remotely operated from Bengaluru using satellite communication. The location's dry, cloud-free conditions and minimal light pollution make it ideal for astronomical observations. The observatory studies stars, galaxies, and transients including supernovae and gamma-ray bursts. It is part of India's growing network of high-altitude research facilities.
fact: It is one of the world's highest observatories at 4,500 meters in Hanle, Ladakh · It houses the 2-meter Himalayan Chandra Telescope · The telescope is remotely operated from Bengaluru · Its dry, cloud-free location is ideal for astronomy

desc: Vainu Bappu Observatory is a major astronomical observatory located in the Javadi Hills of Tamil Nadu, near Kavalur. It was established in 1967 and is operated by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics. The observatory houses India's largest optical telescope, the 2.3-meter Vainu Bappu Telescope, named after the renowned Indian astronomer. It also has a 1-meter telescope and a 75-cm reflector telescope. The observatory has contributed significantly to studies of comets, binary stars, and stellar spectroscopy. The site is known for its dark skies and moderate atmospheric turbulence.
fact: It houses India's largest optical telescope, the 2.3-meter Vainu Bappu Telescope · It was established in 1967 in the Javadi Hills, Tamil Nadu · It is operated by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics · It has contributed to studies of comets, binary stars, and stellar spectroscopy

desc: The Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT) is one of the world's largest and most sensitive radio telescopes, located near Narayangaon, Pune. It was built in 1995 and is operated by the National Centre for Radio Astrophysics of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research. The telescope consists of 30 fully steerable parabolic dishes, each 45 meters in diameter, spread over an area of 25 km. GMRT observes radio waves from celestial objects including pulsars, galaxies, and cosmic hydrogen. It has made significant discoveries in astrophysics including studies of the early universe and gravitational lensing. The telescope is undergoing major upgrades to increase its sensitivity.
fact: It is one of the world's largest radio telescopes with 30 dishes of 45 meters each · It was built in 1995 near Pune, Maharashtra · It studies pulsars, galaxies, and cosmic hydrogen · It is operated by NCRA-TIFR and is undergoing major sensitivity upgrades

desc: Jantar Mantar in Jaipur is a collection of 19 astronomical instruments built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II between 1727 and 1734. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most significant observatories in the world. The instruments include the world's largest stone sundial, the Samrat Yantra, standing 27 meters tall. The observatory was designed to measure time, track celestial bodies, and predict eclipses using naked-eye observations. The instruments are built from local stone and marble with precise geometric alignments. Jantar Mantar represents the pinnacle of pre-telescope astronomical instruments and is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture.
fact: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with 19 astronomical instruments built in 1727-34 · It has the world's largest stone sundial, the Samrat Yantra at 27 meters · It was built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II · It represents the pinnacle of pre-telescope astronomical instruments
